summary: Baie Ellis range lights guide ships into Ellis Bay at Port-Menier, Anticosti: first lit 11 August 1906 for Henri Menier; towers moved 1927; later dates disputed.

lens.note: Historic front light: fixed white dioptric, fourth order (Department report, year ended 30 June 1907)

structures.note: 33 ft from foundation to vane (1907 report); moved 1927; LighthouseFriends says it survives in the woods
52 ft (1907 report); stone masonry foundation; lowered and moved 1989 (LighthouseFriends; Quebec society says it stayed in place)

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Rear tower beside the Menier chateau ruins on Chemin du Château; front tower reportedly in the woods off Chemin de la Baie-Sainte-Claire.

facts.agency: Port-Menier (historic rear tower, per LighthouseFriends); Canadian Coast Guard (current range lights, per its List of Lights)

events.note: Two range lights ordered from Sautter & Harle; pieces arrived 1905 and the front light was erected that year (LighthouseFriends). The Quebec society dates construction to 1904.
Both range lights first lit 11 August 1906 (LighthouseFriends)
Steamer Montcalm, sailing 28 February with freight for Ellis Bay, could not reach it because of packed ice; back in Quebec 5 March 1917
Tidal observations at Ellis Bay with the Hydrographic Survey
Cast-iron towers moved to a new alignment at the head of the bay because of wharf modifications (LighthouseFriends)
Historic range lights decommissioned 'some time after 1985' (LighthouseFriends); modern range lights in service
Rear tower lowered from its crumbling base, moved to a new foundation near the Menier chateau, lantern replaced with the front tower's (LighthouseFriends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's conflict over whether the light is still lit is resolved by the Coast Guard's list, which gives current front and rear range lights at the bay, and by LighthouseFriends, which says the modern range lights remain in operation. The historic 1906 towers were decommissioned after 1985.

Construction is dated 1904 by the Quebec society and 1905 by LighthouseFriends (front light erected that year), with the range first lit on 11 August 1906 (LighthouseFriends). The record's 1906 entry matches the lighting date.

notes_for_editor: 1) Construction: Les amis des phares (cite 7) gives 1904; LighthouseFriends (cite 1) gives the pieces arriving and the front light erected in 1905, rear-light work from July 1906, first lit 11 August 1906. The story gives both. 2) Menier's death: LighthouseFriends gives 1915 (cite 1). A Montreal history site (cite 8, French, secondary) gives 1913 and attributes it to the Commission de toponymie du Quebec. The commission's own record pages (toponymie.gouv.qc.ca) are client-rendered and returned no text through fetch_text, so they are not cited. Unresolved; the story states both. 3) Sale: LighthouseFriends gives 1926 to the Anticosti Corporation (cite 1). The Anticosti tourism timeline gives 1908 (cite 10). Hamelin's 1980 study title ends the Menier period in 1926 (cite 9). Unresolved; the story states both. 4) Rear tower: LighthouseFriends says it was lowered and dragged to a new site in winter 1989 and set on a new foundation in summer 1990 (cite 1). The Quebec society says it stayed at its original place (cite 7). Unresolved. 5) Front tower: LighthouseFriends and the Quebec society both place what remains in the woods along the road to Baie-Sainte-Claire. A LighthouseFriends reader note about a rusted metal object near the chateau was a support column and is not used. 6) LighthouseFriends attributes its 1907-report-style description to the 1906 report; the text checked is the Department's Annual Report for the year ended 30 June 1907 (scan p. 41, printed p. 34, read by page lookup). 7) Units: the 1907 report gives ranges in 'miles' without 'nautical', so they are printed as the source gives them. Heights are converted metres first. 8) The Department's 1906-series volume (corpus marine_ca 1905, 1906v40i9p21_0345) calls Martin-Zede Menier's 'representative'; the story uses LighthouseFriends' wording ('his friend', 'leadership') and does not cite that volume. 9) The 1900 report's Menier passage (scan p. 56, printed p. 41) and the 1917 Montcalm passage (scan p. 68, printed p. 61) are cited by page lookup; neither was matched from an OCR table. 10) LighthouseFriends' 1974 sale price and buyer are not used. No keeper is named for the range in any source read, so the roster is empty. 11) The Coast Guard list is cited for the current names only; its height figures are not used. 12) Confidence stays medium: two sources disagree on each of the construction year, the death year, the sale year and the 1989 move.
